method:
Corpus: all 280 evalset items (IR plus reference solution; current verdicts from denetim/2026-10-01/d4/fark_782431c.json: 155 CORRECT, 125 INCORRECT) and the 278 recorded K4 AI solutions (reports/arsiv/2026-09-28/solver_meta_results.json, read the way fark.py reads them; 274 CORRECT, 4 INCORRECT). It contains only 86 distinct IRs. I also used the 89 'ders kitabı' (textbook) cases of d4e round 4 (scr/d4/duzeltme/d4e/r4/q/kap.py and kap2.py). Their current verdicts come from kap_eski.txt and kap2_eski.txt, measured on a0a0829, whose src is identical to edison's (git diff a0a0829 edison -- src is empty): 64 CORRECT, 23 UNKNOWN, 2 INCORRECT. The d4e4 verdicts come from kap_now.txt and kap2_now.txt.

The ~95 inventory findings were deduplicated into 29 candidate rules plus 2 no-rule rows (X1 exact wip fixes, X2 already-UNKNOWN), and each finding ID appears in exactly one row. Each rule got a static trigger (regex with paren-aware call parsing over IR params, givens, functions, options, answer payloads and step claims) in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-asd/f97a07bd-dea8-5bbe-88dc-ada419b43e01/scratchpad/wf/realist/scan.py. Output is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-asd/f97a07bd-dea8-5bbe-88dc-ada419b43e01/scratchpad/wf/realist/scan_out.json and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-asd/f97a07bd-dea8-5bbe-88dc-ada419b43e01/scratchpad/wf/realist/scan_final.txt. Hits are counted as unique evalset items, K4 solutions and textbook cases, with the current verdict of each hit.

'Would lose CORRECT' was settled in three ways:
(a) For rules already implemented in a wip branch, the recorded full verdict diffs of the 558 solutions against 782431c (all 0/0/0/0): 9d60d17 (d4b NOTLAR.md:257), c32cdad (d4c NOTLAR.md:281-282), 9561c9a (d4e NOTLAR.md:349), a2f5603 (d4h NOTLAR.md:94).
(b) Seven targeted probe runs, each in its own git-archive copy, all deleted afterwards. probe_rp.py is a pure-SymPy replica of sym_equal and zero_test_battery on every currently CORRECT expression-shaped unit. probe_tb.py ran 13 textbook cases on 9d60d17 and 18 plus 4 on c32cdad. probe_units.py ran 41 corpus units on 1aa422f (d4h round 2 is not diff-measured; verdict, first bad step and step statuses were compared with fark_782431c) and 7 extremum units on c32cdad. Every probed unit gave the same result as edison, except one gain: ∫₀^∞ sin t/t on c32cdad.
(c) For unimplemented rules, analysis of the trigger hits. Examples: the K4 traces show certify.algebra also passing where wordproblem passes; verify time comes from the trace field 'Toplam süre', not the record's 'ms', which is solver API time.

Bottom line: on the 558 realistic corpus solutions, no candidate rule removes a currently CORRECT verdict in the form already implemented or in the narrow reading of its wording.
Textbook costs exist only for broad variants:
- D4E4-YO-2 as worded: −1 edison CORRECT (√(sin x)′), −1 d4e4 gain (√(1+cos x)′), 2 unclear (parametric cases).
- D4C-T4-PI if implemented naively: −2 (√(x³)′ and (x³)^(1/3)′ with x > 0); 0 if the symbolic identity is proved on the comparison region.
- Hard timeout: 0 at a limit of 20 s or more; 14 K4 at 10 s.
The wide reading of D4H-YO-1 would also create 6 new false CORRECTs on cell-D evalset items, which is a soundness risk, not a coverage one.
caveats:
1. Static triggers are approximations. Several rules fire only on internal events (an exception in an intersection, a budget running out, an unreadable as-written text) that regex cannot see, so those counts are upper bounds; R27's trigger is especially crude. Rows with 0 hits can also mean my pattern missed a form, but every 0-hit class was also spot-checked against claims_dump.txt.
2. The corpus is narrow: 86 distinct IRs, about 25 problem templates, and K4 comes from one solver model (muse-spark-1.3) whose answers are almost all set, interval or number forms with sympy-syntax steps and no LaTeX. A 0 here means 'not in this corpus', not 'not realistic'. Realistic classes absent from it: chained or compound givens (0 < x < 3), domain lists or 'x ∉ [a,b]', arithmetic-sequence 'd', AI general solutions with two family indices, decimal-comma options, √ of trig in a derivative, parametric improper integrals.
3. Textbook verdicts are from the recorded kap files, not re-run on edison. The d4e4 column (kap_now) for acos(1−2x²)′ is stale: d7b0367 gives INCORRECT, while 1a82e0c gives UNKNOWN per d4e NOTLAR.md:335-337.
4. K4 verify times come from the 2026-09-28 traces (older code, cloud machine); current code may be slower. The evalset figure is the 223 ms mean from reports/eval_report.md, not per item.
5. d4h round 2 (1aa422f) and d4b round 10 (9d60d17) are in progress. 9d60d17 has a full diff (0); 1aa422f has only my 41-unit targeted probe, all SAME, not a full diff.
6. D4E4-YO-2/YO-3 (R12b), D4C-T4-PI naive vs region proof (R08), R09 widened, R10 and R29 are analytical judgments about rules that do not exist in code. For R12b the two parametric textbook cases are marked unclear because the rule wording does not say whether a parametric zero counts as classified.
7. probe_rp.py replicates the verifier's symbolic path in plain SymPy 1.14 with real=True symbols. It does not run the verifier's own kink_reading/_sign_off pipeline, so a CORRECT reached through another internal route could be misclassified. The 2 'random point needed' cases were cross-checked: simplify(diff − claim) ≠ 0 over ℝ, and = 0 after substituting x = t with t > 0.
8. I used 7 of the 8 allowed runs (counting the pure-SymPy probe). All copies were removed; nothing was written outside /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-asd/f97a07bd-dea8-5bbe-88dc-ada419b43e01/scratchpad/wf/realist/, and nothing was pushed.
